info.name: Zapper Assignment Demo
info.description: Ordered local demo flows for Zapper API and Acme stub. Start the local stack first. Run requests in order within each folder; variables are generated and passed between requests automatically. Stub control endpoints are development-only simulator controls. No card data is included.

item.name: 00 - Readiness and reset
item.description: Start with `docker compose up --build -d --wait` from the repository root, or start PostgreSQL and Seq then launch Visual Studio's `Zapper + Acme Stub` profile. Local ports: API 5280, stub 5291.

exec: pm.test('Zapper database is ready', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });
pm.test('Acme stub is healthy', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });

item.name: Reset Acme default scenario to Approved
01 - Approved payment and idempotency
item.description: Run requests in order: approve, capture the provider transaction ID, query Zapper, replay the exact same request, then change one field under the same appPaymentId to see the conflict.

exec: pm.test('Unique demo transaction found', function () { pm.expect(m.length).to.eql(1); });
pm.test('Payment lookup is approved', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); pm.expect(pm.response.json().status).to.eql('Approved'); });

request.description: Same ID and same body should replay the stored result without creating another provider transaction.

exec: pm.test('Exact replay returns stored payment', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); pm.expect(pm.response.json().appPaymentId).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('approvalAppPaymentId')); });
pm.test('Changed request rejected as idempotency conflict', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(409); pm.expect(pm.response.json().code).to.eql('IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT'); });

item.name: 02 - Decline and pending PEND
item.description: Demonstrates a business decline and the asynchronous PEND flow. Zapper first records Processing/PEND; the stub outcome is then changed to Approved, it sends a Payment Advice callback, and Zapper moves the payment to Approved.

request.description: Acme returns Processing/PEND; Zapper stores local status Processing.

exec: pm.test('PEND is represented as Processing', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(202); pm.expect(pm.response.json().status).to.eql('Processing'); pm.expect(pm.response.json().acmeResponseCode).to.eql('PEND'); });

var n=Number(pm.collectionVariables.get('pendingAmount')); var m=pm.response.json().filter(function(t){return Number(t.amount)===n;}); pm.test('Pending stub transaction found', function(){pm.expect(m.length).to.eql(1);}); if(m.length)pm.collectionVariables.set('pendingTransactionId',m[0].transactionId);

item.name: Change pending provider transaction to Approved

request.description: Updates this already-created provider transaction, so the following callback carries Success/00. It does not create a new payment.
Stub sends an authenticated Payment Advice callback with Success/00 to Zapper. No manual callback credentials are needed.

exec: pm.test('Stub delivered approval advice', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); pm.expect(pm.response.json().deliveries[0].statusCode).to.eql(200); });

pm.test('Payment Advice moved payment to Approved', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); pm.expect(pm.response.json().status).to.eql('Approved'); pm.expect(pm.response.json().acmeResponseCode).to.eql('00'); });

item.name: 03 - Payment Advice, refund, and reversal callbacks
item.description: Self-contained notification demo: create an approved payment, capture its Acme transaction ID, send duplicate and stale Payment Advice, apply a partial refund, then create a second approved payment and reverse it. The stub sends authenticated/signed callbacks to Zapper.

item.name: Create approved payment for advice and refund

exec: pm.test('Callback source payment is approved', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(201); pm.expect(pm.response.json().status).to.eql('Approved'); });

var n=Number(pm.collectionVariables.get('callbackBaseAmount')); var m=pm.response.json().filter(function(t){return Number(t.amount)===n;}); pm.test('Advice/refund transaction found', function(){pm.expect(m.length).to.eql(1);}); if(m.length)pm.collectionVariables.set('callbackBaseTransactionId',m[0].transactionId);

request.description: Sends the same advice callback twice to Zapper.

exec: pm.test('Stub sent two successful callback deliveries', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); var d=pm.response.json().deliveries; pm.expect(d.length).to.eql(2); pm.expect(d.every(function(x){return x.statusCode===200;})).to.eql(true); });

request.description: Sends advice with an old provider timestamp to exercise stale notification handling.

exec: pm.test('Stub delivered stale advice to Zapper', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); pm.expect(pm.response.json().deliveries[0].statusCode).to.eql(200); });

request.description: Stub signs and delivers a partial refund callback using a generated amount in minor currency units; original payment must be approved.

exec: pm.test('Stub delivered refund callback to Zapper', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); pm.expect(pm.response.json().statusCode).to.eql(200); });
pm.test('Partial refund is reflected on the payment', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); pm.expect(pm.response.json().status).to.eql('PartiallyRefunded'); });

item.name: Submit separate approved payment for reversal

exec: pm.test('Separate original payment approved', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(201); pm.expect(pm.response.json().status).to.eql('Approved'); });

var n=Number(pm.collectionVariables.get('reversalAmount')); var m=pm.response.json().filter(function(t){return Number(t.amount)===n;}); pm.test('Reversal transaction found', function(){pm.expect(m.length).to.eql(1);}); if(m.length)pm.collectionVariables.set('reversalTransactionId',m[0].transactionId);

request.description: Stub signs and delivers a full reversal callback for a separate approved payment.

exec: pm.test('Reversal is reflected on the payment', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); pm.expect(pm.response.json().status).to.eql('Reversed'); });

item.name: 04 - Timeout and reconciliation
item.description: The API call takes about the configured eight-second timeout. The stub records the transaction but drops the submission response. Zapper's timeout reconciliation query finds it as Processing/PEND; then change that stored provider result to Approved and use GET to reconcile again.

exec: pm.test('Timed-out submission is reconciled as provider pending', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(202); pm.expect(pm.response.json().status).to.eql('Processing'); pm.expect(pm.response.json().acmeResponseCode).to.eql('PEND'); });

var n=Number(pm.collectionVariables.get('timeoutAmount')); var m=pm.response.json().filter(function(t){return Number(t.amount)===n;}); pm.test('Timeout transaction found', function(){pm.expect(m.length).to.eql(1);}); if(m.length)pm.collectionVariables.set('timeoutTransactionId',m[0].transactionId);
pm.test('Existing payment reconciled to Approved', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); pm.expect(pm.response.json().status).to.eql('Approved'); });

item.name: 05 - E29 throttling and manual retry
item.description: Queue two throttles. Zapper automatically retries once; the first POST should return E29. Repeat the exact same POST with the same ID and amount to perform the supported manual retry.

item.name: Submit payment (expect E29 after automatic retry)

exec: pm.test('E29 returned after automatic retry', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(503); pm.expect(pm.response.json().code).to.eql('E29'); });

item.name: Manual retry with same ID and body

exec: pm.test('E29 manual retry approved', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(201); pm.expect(pm.response.json().status).to.eql('Approved'); });

item.name: 06 - E50 gateway failure
item.description: Demonstrates Acme's E50 gateway failure and restores the normal default scenario afterward.

exec: pm.test('Gateway failure is E50', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(502); pm.expect(pm.response.json().code).to.eql('E50'); });

item.name: 07 - RRN collision (direct Acme stub)
item.description: Zapper generates a fresh RRN per payment, so demonstrate the provider collision rule by calling Acme directly. Run the preparation and two POSTs in order. The requests share a 12-digit OrderNumber prefix but use different TransactionIDs.

exec: pm.test('First provider request succeeds', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); pm.expect(pm.response.json().PaymentResponse.ResponseDetail.Code).to.eql('00'); });

item.name: Submit second Acme payment (expect E09 collision)

exec: pm.test('RRN collision returns HTTP 409', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(409); });

pm.test('RRN collision returns E09 and original transaction ID', function () { var r=pm.response.json().PaymentResponse; pm.expect(r.ResponseDetail.Code).to.eql('E09'); pm.expect(r.TransactionID).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('collisionFirstTransactionId')); });

item.name: 08 - Provider query and daily report
item.description: Self-contained closing demo: create and capture an approved payment for the authenticated Acme RTQ query, then request today's Zapper daily settlement summary. Seq UI is at http://localhost:5341.

item.name: Create approved payment for provider query

exec: pm.test('Provider query source payment is approved', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(201); pm.expect(pm.response.json().status).to.eql('Approved'); });

var n=Number(pm.collectionVariables.get('queryAmount')); var m=pm.response.json().filter(function(t){return Number(t.amount)===n;}); pm.test('Query transaction found', function(){pm.expect(m.length).to.eql(1);}); if(m.length)pm.collectionVariables.set('queryTransactionId',m[0].transactionId);

pm.test('Acme RTQ returned the transaction', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); pm.expect(pm.response.json().PaymentResponse.TransactionID).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('queryTransactionId')); });
